font-family:'Times New Roman Cyr';-inkscape-font-specification:'Times New Roman Cyr';text-align:start

tspan.tspan: . The XAS setup involves an X-ray source generating a beam that interacts with the sample positioned

tspan.style: font-family:'Times New Roman Cyr';-inkscape-font-specification:'Times New Roman Cyr';text-align:start

tspan.tspan: on a sample holder. A mosaic crystal directs the transmitted beam through a slit system (S1 and S2) for collimation, and a pixel

tspan.style: font-family:'Times New Roman Cyr';-inkscape-font-specification:'Times New Roman Cyr';text-align:start

tspan.tspan: detector records the signal. In the XES setup, the X-ray source excites the sample, leading to the emission of fluorescence X-rays.

tspan.style: font-family:'Times New Roman Cyr';-inkscape-font-specification:'Times New Roman Cyr';text-align:start

tspan.tspan: These emitted X-rays are analyzed by a mosaic crystal, collimated through the slit system (S1 and S2), and detected by a pixel detector, enabling the study of emission properties.
